traceability.notes:
The ESLint configuration story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG appears fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are covered: - Core Functionality: src/index.ts defines `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` as ESLint v9 flat-config arrays of rule severities. Integration tests (tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts) use these presets with FlatESLint and confirm that traceability rules (e.g., `traceability/require-story-annotation`) are enabled, matching REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS. - Quality Standards (ESLint v9 flat config): The plugin exposes flat config arrays intended to be spread into consumer configs; tests use ESLint’s `FlatESLint` API, and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md demonstrates proper flat-config patterns. No legacy `.eslintrc`-specific behavior is required. - Integration: Flat-config presets are designed to be composed with other configs (e.g., `@eslint/js` recommended). The integration tests build combined configs `[baseConfig, ...configs.recommended]` and run ESLint successfully, showing no conflicts with existing configuration. - User Experience & Documentation: The ESLint 9 Setup Guide and README provide clear examples for JavaScript-only, TypeScript, mixed JS/TS, monorepo, config files, and test files. There is also a troubleshooting section that addresses common ESLint flat-config pitfalls. This satisfies the documentation-oriented acceptance criteria. - Error Handling & Config Validation: Rule schemas in src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts and src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts declare allowed options and set `additionalProperties: false`. Tests in tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts assert that ESLint throws informative errors for unknown options and invalid types, and reference REQ-RULE-OPTIONS and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION. The valid-story-reference rule and its tests further demonstrate configurable story directories, absolute path controls, and extension handling (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS).
All story requirements (REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG, REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION, REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION) have concrete implementation and passing tests, and documentation exists for setup and troubleshooting. The latest test run shows all relevant config tests passing, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
